identity.name: NGFW EAL Rare-Domain Beacon then Large/Massive HTTPS Upload Exfil — Cortex Network Analytics / ABIOC (T1071.001 / T1048 / T1567)
identity.summary: A host beacons at a recurring interval to a rare domain over HTTPS, then uploads a large then massive data volume to a rare storage/mail domain. No IP or domain is a known-bad IOC — the deviation from the host's learned NGFW EAL egress baseline (destination rarity, recurring cadence, anomalous bytes_sent) is what the auto-tuned Cortex NGFW Analytics / ABIOC detectors fire on.
identity.description: The PAN-OS NGFW Enhanced Application Logs (EAL) carry per-session application, byte-volume and URL/domain context that Cortex XSIAM Network Security Analytics learns a per-host egress baseline from. EAL records land in the primary NGFW traffic dataset panw_ngfw_traffic_raw (log_source_type = "eal" isolates the EAL subset within that traffic dataset). This card exercises the three NGFW EAL analytics alerts named in the XSIAM Analytics Alert Reference for that data source against a single beacon-then-exfil chain, all keyed on panw_ngfw_traffic_raw: (1) Abnormal Recurring Communications to a Rare Domain — a regular-interval burst of small HTTPS (ssl/443) sessions from one source to a domain that is rare across the fleet (few distinct sources ever contact it), the C2-beacon shape that survives infrastructure rotation because no address is a static IOC; (2) Large Upload (HTTPS) — a single session whose bytes_sent over 443 is anomalously large versus the host's learned outbound-volume baseline; and (3) Massive upload to a rare storage or mail domain — a subsequent, even larger bytes_sent to a rare object-store / mail domain, the exfiltration terminal of the chain. Because a domain-blocklist or IOC rule keyed on a specific address misses the beacon the moment infrastructure rotates and never sees the volume anomaly at all, the signal that matters is behavioral and lives entirely in the network plane: destination rarity (fleet-wide source prevalence), recurring cadence, and outbound-byte anomaly, each a deviation from what Cortex has learned is normal for the host. Two ABIOCs anchor the recurring-beacon and massive-upload deviations to the source host (src) and rare destination domain (rare destination -> recurring small callbacks -> anomalous upload volume from the same source host); a third statistical ABIOC covers the large-HTTPS-upload volume deviation; two validation XQL queries prove the emitted panw_ngfw_traffic_raw records landed and surface each deviation; and a correlation rule stitches the recurring-beacon ABIOC and the massive-upload ABIOC for the same source host into one beacon-then-exfil incident that a static domain/IOC rule would never have raised. The scenario drives the ngfw_eal_emitter analytics log-streamer to POST shape-true panw_ngfw_traffic_raw records into an operator-supplied collector, so a customer validates that these NGFW Analytics / ABIOC detections fire without generating a single real outbound session to a rare domain or storage endpoint.

campaigns: Large-volume HTTPS exfiltration to attacker-controlled object storage

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-NDR-012 — NGFW EAL rare-domain recurring beacon then large/massive HTTPS upload exfil, driven by the ngfw_eal_emitter analytics log-streamer for Cortex NGFW Analytics / ABIOC validation.

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP collector already wired into Cortex XSIAM as a PAN-OS NGFW EAL third-party source so posted records reach the panw_ngfw_traffic_raw dataset.
prerequisites.check_command: python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli describe ngfw_eal_emitter | jq -e '.eal_targets | length > 0'

prerequisites.description: A baseline window has elapsed during which the source host produced only its normal egress so Cortex Network Security Analytics learned the host egress profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad IOC. Drive the ngfw_eal_emitter analytics log-streamer to POST
# shape-true panw_ngfw_traffic_raw records: a recurring rare-domain HTTPS beacon,
# then a large HTTPS upload, then a massive upload to a rare storage/mail domain.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/ngfw/eal/events}"
for PATTERN in abnormal_recurring_comms large_upload_https massive_upload_rare_domain; do
  python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run-plugin ngfw_eal_emitter \
    --param collector_url="${COLLECTOR_URL}" \
    --param event_pattern="${PATTERN}" \
    --live || true
done

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP collector wired into XSIAM as the PAN-OS NGFW EAL source.

expected_artifacts.description: A recurring, regular-interval burst of small HTTPS (ssl/443) sessions from one source to a domain that is rare for the host.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: app = "ssl" AND dst_port = 443 AND recurring_sessions >= 6 AND fleet_src_prevalence <= 2

expected_artifacts.description: A large then massive bytes_sent HTTPS upload to a rare storage or mail domain from the same source host.

abiocs.name: NGFW EAL — Abnormal Recurring Communications to a Rare Domain
abiocs.description: A source host produces a tight, recurring burst of small HTTPS (ssl/443) sessions to a single domain that is rare across the fleet (few distinct sources ever contact it) — the rare-domain C2-beacon shape. Every destination is legitimate-looking and rotates, so no IOC matches; the ABIOC fires on the recurring-cadence-plus-destination-rarity deviation from the host's learned NGFW EAL egress baseline, anchored to the source host (src) and the rare destination domain rather than to a known-bad indicator.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and app = "ssl" and dst_port = 443
| filter action = "allow"
| comp count() as recurring_sessions, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes by src, url_domain
| windowcomp count_distinct(src) as fleet_src_prevalence by url_domain
| filter recurring_sessions >= 6 and avg_bytes < 8192 and fleet_src_prevalence <= 2
| sort desc recurring_sessions
| fields src, url_domain, recurring_sessions, avg_bytes, fleet_src_prevalence
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host NGFW EAL egress baseline (few destinations, ordinary bursty web volume) -> a single domain that is rare across the fleet (low distinct-source prevalence) contacted at a recurring interval with small stable payloads, anchored to the source host (src) and that rare destination domain.

abiocs.name: NGFW EAL — Large Upload (HTTPS) to a Rare Domain
abiocs.description: A single HTTPS (ssl/443) session carries a bytes_sent volume that is anomalously large versus the host's learned outbound-volume baseline, to a domain that is rare across the fleet. The statistical ABIOC fires on the outbound-byte-volume deviation, the first stage of the exfiltration that follows the rare-domain beacon, anchored to the source host (src) and the rare destination domain.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and app = "ssl" and dst_port = 443 and action = "allow"
| filter bytes_sent > 1073741824
| comp sum(bytes_sent) as uploaded_bytes, count() as sessions by src, url_domain
| windowcomp count_distinct(src) as fleet_src_prevalence by url_domain
| filter uploaded_bytes > 1073741824 and fleet_src_prevalence <= 2
| sort desc uploaded_bytes
| fields src, url_domain, uploaded_bytes, sessions, fleet_src_prevalence
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host outbound-volume baseline over 443 -> a single session whose bytes_sent is a large positive deviation to a fleet-rare domain, anchored to the source host (src) and destination domain.

abiocs.name: NGFW EAL — Massive Upload to a Rare Storage or Mail Domain
abiocs.description: The same source host uploads a massive bytes_sent volume to a storage / mail domain that is rare across the fleet over HTTPS — the exfiltration terminal of the beacon-then-exfil chain. The ABIOC fires on the massive-outbound-volume-to-a-rare-domain deviation from the learned baseline, anchored to the same source host (src) that carried the earlier recurring beacon.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and dst_port = 443 and action = "allow"
| filter bytes_sent > 10737418240
| comp sum(bytes_sent) as uploaded_bytes, count() as sessions by src, url_domain
| windowcomp count_distinct(src) as fleet_src_prevalence by url_domain
| filter uploaded_bytes > 10737418240 and fleet_src_prevalence <= 2
| sort desc uploaded_bytes
| fields src, url_domain, uploaded_bytes, fleet_src_prevalence
abiocs.causality_anchor: Recurring rare-domain beacon under the source host (src) -> a massive bytes_sent upload to a fleet-rare storage or mail domain from that same source host, anchored to the src egress chain that generated the beacon.

xql_queries.name: NGFW EAL — Recurring Rare-Domain Beacon Landed in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and app = "ssl" and dst_port = 443
| comp count() as recurring_sessions, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes by src, url_domain
| filter recurring_sessions >= 6
| fields src, url_domain, recurring_sessions, avg_bytes

xql_queries.name: NGFW EAL — Large and Massive HTTPS Upload Landed in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter log_source_type = "eal" and dst_port = 443 and action = "allow"
| filter bytes_sent > 1073741824
| comp max(bytes_sent) as peak_upload_bytes, sum(bytes_sent) as total_upload_bytes by src, url_domain
| sort desc peak_upload_bytes
| fields src, url_domain, peak_upload_bytes, total_upload_bytes

correlation_rules.name: NGFW EAL Rare-Domain Beacon then Massive Upload — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(NGFW EAL — Abnormal Recurring Communications to a Rare Domain) AND ABIOC(NGFW EAL — Massive Upload to a Rare Storage or Mail Domain) — fuses the recurring rare-domain HTTPS beacon and the subsequent massive upload from the same NGFW EAL source host (src) into one beacon-then-exfil incident anchored to that shared source host: recurring rare-domain callbacks over 443 lead to a large then massive bytes_sent upload to a fleet-rare storage or mail domain from the same source host, surviving destination/IP rotation that defeats any static IOC.

threat_scenarios.name: NGFW EAL Rare-Domain Beacon then Large/Massive HTTPS Upload Exfil via Cortex Network Analytics / ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned NGFW EAL Network Analytics / ABIOCs learn a host's egress baseline and detect a recurring rare-domain HTTPS beacon and the large-then-massive HTTPS upload that follows by their destination rarity (fleet-wide source prevalence), recurring cadence and outbound-byte-volume deviation, anchored to the source host (src) and rare destination domain, after infrastructure rotation defeats any static IOC.

threat_steps.objective: The recurring rare-domain HTTPS beacon fires the Abnormal Recurring Communications to a Rare Domain ABIOC and its validation XQL surfaces the landed panw_ngfw_traffic_raw records.
preconditions: Operator collector wired into XSIAM as the PAN-OS NGFW EAL source (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw populated).
Baseline window elapsed with the source host producing only its normal egress.
steps: Let the host egress baseline window elapse.
success_criteria: ABIOC `NGFW EAL — Abnormal Recurring Communications to a Rare Domain` fires.
Validation XQL returns the recurring rare-domain sessions in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw.

threat_steps.objective: The large HTTPS upload fires the Large Upload (HTTPS) ABIOC on the outbound-byte-volume deviation.
preconditions: Recurring beacon (TS-NDR-012A) already established the rare-domain callback pattern.
success_criteria: ABIOC `NGFW EAL — Large Upload (HTTPS) to a Rare Domain` fires.
Upload validation XQL surfaces the anomalous bytes_sent session in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw.

threat_steps.objective: The massive upload fires the Massive upload to a rare storage or mail domain ABIOC and the correlation stitches the beacon-then-exfil chain into one incident.
preconditions: Large upload (TS-NDR-012B) already demonstrated the outbound-volume deviation.
steps: Observe the massive-upload ABIOC fire and the correlation raise one incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `NGFW EAL — Massive Upload to a Rare Storage or Mail Domain` fires.
Correlation `CR-NDR-0012` raises one stitched beacon-then-exfil incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce App-ID least-privilege egress and require an authenticated egress proxy so hosts cannot reach arbitrary rare domains or object-store endpoints directly.
Block newly-registered / high-entropy domains and apply outbound data-volume policy on egress NGFW so large/massive HTTPS uploads to rare domains are throttled or denied, not merely detected.
Apply Advanced Threat Prevention, Advanced URL Filtering and DNS Security on all outbound web traffic.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune NGFW EAL network ABIOCs against the learned per-host egress baseline rather than hand-authoring IOC rules for individual C2 or storage domains that rotate.
Baseline per-host destination cardinality, callback cadence and outbound byte-volume; alert on recurring small sessions to a rare domain and on anomalously large bytes_sent.

Correlate the recurring rare-domain beacon and the subsequent massive upload for one source host into a single beacon-then-exfil incident anchored to the shared source host (src) and rare destination domains.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Promoted from research-intake scaffold to active NGFW EAL network Analytics/ABIOC card — rare-domain recurring HTTPS beacon then large/massive HTTPS upload exfil (three XSIAM NGFW EAL analytics alerts), three ABIOCs + two validation XQL stitched by CR-NDR-0012. Keyed on the real primary NGFW traffic dataset panw_ngfw_traffic_raw (EAL enrichment isolated via log_source_type = "eal"); rarity computed as fleet-wide distinct-source prevalence per url_domain; recurring beacon anchored on T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols). Anchored on the pure network-plane keys src + url_domain (no endpoint-process fields, which NGFW EAL does not carry). Driven by the ngfw_eal_emitter analytics log-streamer. Backs scenario SIM-NDR-012.
